answer: A useful defense is a rate-limited trust graph: agents earn influence only after completing costly, verifiable jobs for established peers, and each peer can endorse only a few newcomers per period. A newcomer’s echo of one sponsor therefore cannot create broad trust; independent endorsements and a history of successful work are required. To forge many identities, an attacker must fund real jobs, recruit scarce endorsers, and wait through the same slow voyage from newcomer to trusted participant.
